$comment: What the `novnc/` directory beside this file is, where it came from, and proof it has not
been changed. Read by packages/scrape/tests/test_operator_assets.py, which recomputes
`tree_sha256` and fails if the tree and this record disagree.
This exists because noVNC is MPL-2.0 and 3tears-scrape is MIT. Redistributing MPL-2.0 files
inside an MIT wheel is permitted, and the obligations are specific: the licence text and
copyright notice travel with the files, the files stay under their own licence regardless of
the wheel's, the source stays identifiable, and any modification is marked. The first two are
satisfied by shipping the upstream LICENSE.txt, AUTHORS and docs/LICENSE.* unmodified next to
the code. The last two are satisfied here -- and `modified: false` is a claim a test can
falsify rather than a promise, which is the only reason it is worth writing down.
Nothing under `novnc/` is ours. The operator page is a SIBLING of that directory rather than
a file inside it, so no file under it can be read as a modified noVNC file.
name: noVNC
tree_sha256_recipe: sha256 over every file under novnc/, sorted by POSIX-relative path, each contributing its path bytes, a NUL, its contents, and a NUL

$comment: Not the whole distribution. `core/` imports nothing outside itself except the pako zlib
modules below, and references no image, stylesheet or translation, so `app/`, `po/`,
`tests/` and noVNC's own vnc.html are not shipped -- the operator page replaces that UI
entirely. Roughly 740K instead of 2.8M.
The two BSD texts are shipped even though nothing in this subset is plainly BSD-licensed,
because the upstream LICENSE.txt shipped beside them names them by path. Dropping them
would leave the notice we are obliged to carry pointing at files that are not there.
vendored_subset.vendor/pako/: zlib in JavaScript; core/inflator.js and core/deflator.js import it
vendored_subset.LICENSE.txt: upstream licence summary and per-part licence map
vendored_subset.AUTHORS: upstream copyright holders, referenced by LICENSE.txt

$comment: Read out of the files rather than copied from upstream's LICENSE.txt summary, because that
summary is stale for this release: it names `core/des.js`, which moved to
`core/crypto/des.js` in 1.7.0, and calls it `Various BSD style licenses` when the file
actually carries two bespoke permissive notices with no SPDX identifier between them.
packages/scrape/pyproject.toml's License-Expression carries these so the wheel's metadata
does not claim the vendored files are MIT.

core/crypto/des.js.why_not_an_spdx_id: two bespoke permissive grants kept intact in the file header -- AT&T Laboratories Cambridge (1999) and Widget Workshop, Inc. (1996). Neither matches a listed SPDX licence, so PEP 639's LicenseRef form is the accurate way to name it.
